#In brief

  • A first-degree (linear) equation can always be reduced to ax+b=0ax + b = 0ax+b=0. If a≠0a \neq 0a=0 it has exactly one solution, x=−bax = -\frac{b}{a}x=−ab​; if a=0a = 0a=0 it is impossible (when b≠0b \neq 0b=0) or it is an identity (when b=0b = 0b=0 as well).
  • Inequalities are solved like equations, with one extra rule: if you multiply or divide by a negative number, the direction of the inequality is reversed (<<< becomes >>> and vice versa).
  • For ax2+bx+c=0ax^2 + bx + c = 0ax2+bx+c=0 first compute the discriminant Δ=b2−4ac\Delta = b^2 - 4acΔ=b2−4ac: two solutions if Δ>0\Delta > 0Δ>0, only one (a double one) if Δ=0\Delta = 0Δ=0, no real solutions if Δ<0\Delta < 0Δ<0. Then use x1,2=−b±Δ2ax_{1,2} = \frac{-b \pm \sqrt{\Delta}}{2a}x1,2​=2a−b±Δ​​.
  • The sum and the product of the solutions, x1+x2=−bax_1 + x_2 = -\frac{b}{a}x1​+x2​=−ab​ and x1x2=cax_1 x_2 = \frac{c}{a}x1​x2​=ac​, let you check a result in a few seconds.
  • For a second-degree (quadratic) inequality think of the parabola: with a>0a > 0a>0 and Δ>0\Delta > 0Δ>0 the trinomial is positive outside the solutions and negative between the solutions.
  • A linear system of two equations is solved by substitution or by elimination; it can have one solution, none (impossible) or infinitely many (indeterminate).
  • The degree of a system is the product of the degrees of its equations.
  • In word problems: choose the unknown, write the equation, solve it and check that the solution makes sense (positive lengths and ages, a whole number of people and so on).

#3.1 First-degree equations and inequalities

#What an equation is

Definition 3.1 Equation and solution

An equation is an equality between two expressions that contains a letter, the unknown (usually xxx). The expression to the left of the equals sign is the left-hand side (primo membro), the one to the right is the right-hand side (secondo membro). A solution is a number that, put in place of xxx, makes the equality true. Solving an equation means finding all its solutions.

For example 2x+1=72x + 1 = 72x+1=7 has the solution x=3x = 3x=3: indeed 2⋅3+1=72 \cdot 3 + 1 = 72⋅3+1=7. The number 111, on the other hand, is not a solution, because 2⋅1+1=3≠72 \cdot 1 + 1 = 3 \neq 72⋅1+1=3=7 (the symbol ≠\neq= is read "is not equal to").

An equation is first-degree (or linear) when, after doing all the calculations, xxx appears only to the first power. It can always be written in the form

ax+b=0ax + b = 0ax+b=0

where aaa and bbb are real numbers. Two equations are equivalent if they have the same solutions: solving means moving from one equation to another one that is equivalent but simpler, until you reach "xxx equals a number".

#The equivalence principles

Rule 3.1 The two equivalence principles
  1. First principle. If you add or subtract the same expression on both sides, you get an equivalent equation.
  2. Second principle. If you multiply or divide both sides by the same non-zero number, you get an equivalent equation.

The two principles give the practical rules you will use all the time:

  • Transposition: a term can move from one side to the other by changing its sign. From 3x−5=73x - 5 = 73x−5=7 you go to 3x=7+53x = 7 + 53x=7+5 (you have added 555 to both sides).
  • Cancellation: a term that is the same on both sides can be removed. In x2+2x=x2+6x^2 + 2x = x^2 + 6x2+2x=x2+6 remove x2x^2x2 from both sides and you are left with 2x=62x = 62x=6.
  • Numerical denominators: multiply all the terms by the least common multiple (lcm) of the denominators and the fractions disappear.
  • Change of sign: multiplying everything by −1-1−1 changes the signs of all the terms, and −x=4-x = 4−x=4 becomes x=−4x = -4x=−4.
Common mistake Multiplying by zero

The second principle holds only with non-zero numbers. Multiplying by 000, any equation becomes 0=00 = 00=0 and you lose all the information. In the same way, you do not divide by an expression that contains xxx (for example by xxx itself) without knowing whether it can be zero: you risk losing solutions.

#Determined, impossible, indeterminate

Once you have reached the form ax+b=0ax + b = 0ax+b=0, that is ax=−bax = -bax=−b, there are three cases.

CoefficientsType of equationSolutions
a≠0a \neq 0a=0determinedexactly one: x=−bax = -\frac{b}{a}x=−ab​
a=0a = 0a=0 and b≠0b \neq 0b=0impossiblenone: it becomes 0⋅x=−b0 \cdot x = -b0⋅x=−b, false for every xxx
a=0a = 0a=0 and b=0b = 0b=0indeterminate (identity)all real numbers: it becomes 0⋅x=00 \cdot x = 00⋅x=0

The set of real numbers is denoted by R\RR; the empty set, i.e. "no solutions", by ∅\emptyset∅.

Method Solving a first-degree equation
  1. Expand the products and remove the brackets.
  2. If there are numerical denominators, multiply every term by their lcm.
  3. Bring the terms with xxx to the left-hand side and the numbers to the right-hand side (transposition, changing the sign).
  4. Add up like terms until you reach ax=−bax = -bax=−b.
  5. If a≠0a \neq 0a=0 divide by aaa; if a=0a = 0a=0 decide whether it is impossible or an identity.
  6. Check (optional but useful): substitute the result into the original equation.
Example 3.1 With brackets: 3(x−4)=5(x−2)+43(x - 4) = 5(x - 2) + 43(x−4)=5(x−2)+4

Expand the products: 3x−12=5x−10+43x - 12 = 5x - 10 + 43x−12=5x−10+4, that is 3x−12=5x−63x - 12 = 5x - 63x−12=5x−6.

Bring the xxx terms to the left and the numbers to the right: 3x−5x=−6+123x - 5x = -6 + 123x−5x=−6+12, so −2x=6-2x = 6−2x=6.

Divide by −2-2−2: x=−3x = -3x=−3.

Check: on the left 3(−3−4)=−213(-3 - 4) = -213(−3−4)=−21, on the right 5(−3−2)+4=−25+4=−215(-3 - 2) + 4 = -25 + 4 = -215(−3−2)+4=−25+4=−21. Correct.

Example 3.2 With denominators: x−14+x6=x+33\frac{x - 1}{4} + \frac{x}{6} = \frac{x + 3}{3}4x−1​+6x​=3x+3​

The lcm of 444, 666 and 333 is 121212. Multiply every term by 121212: 12⋅x−14=3(x−1)12 \cdot \frac{x - 1}{4} = 3(x - 1)12⋅4x−1​=3(x−1), 12⋅x6=2x12 \cdot \frac{x}{6} = 2x12⋅6x​=2x, 12⋅x+33=4(x+3)12 \cdot \frac{x + 3}{3} = 4(x + 3)12⋅3x+3​=4(x+3). You get

3(x−1)+2x=4(x+3)3(x - 1) + 2x = 4(x + 3)3(x−1)+2x=4(x+3)

that is 3x−3+2x=4x+123x - 3 + 2x = 4x + 123x−3+2x=4x+12, then 5x−4x=12+35x - 4x = 12 + 35x−4x=12+3 and finally x=15x = 15x=15.

Check: 144+156=3.5+2.5=6\frac{14}{4} + \frac{15}{6} = 3.5 + 2.5 = 6414​+615​=3.5+2.5=6 and 183=6\frac{18}{3} = 6318​=6.

Example 3.3 An impossible equation and an identity

2(x+3)−x=x+42(x + 3) - x = x + 42(x+3)−x=x+4 becomes 2x+6−x=x+42x + 6 - x = x + 42x+6−x=x+4, that is x+6=x+4x + 6 = x + 4x+6=x+4. Bringing the xxx terms to the left: 0⋅x=−20 \cdot x = -20⋅x=−2. No number multiplied by 000 gives −2-2−2: the equation is impossible.

3(x−1)+2=3x−13(x - 1) + 2 = 3x - 13(x−1)+2=3x−1 becomes 3x−1=3x−13x - 1 = 3x - 13x−1=3x−1, that is 0⋅x=00 \cdot x = 00⋅x=0: true for every xxx. It is an identity and the solution set is R\RR.

Common mistake The minus sign in front of a fraction

In x2−x−34=1\frac{x}{2} - \frac{x - 3}{4} = 12x​−4x−3​=1 the minus sign applies to the whole numerator. Multiplying by 444 you get 2x−(x−3)=42x - (x - 3) = 42x−(x−3)=4, that is 2x−x+3=42x - x + 3 = 42x−x+3=4, and so x=1x = 1x=1. Writing 2x−x−3=42x - x - 3 = 42x−x−3=4 is the most common mistake (it would lead to x=7x = 7x=7). And remember that multiplying by 444 applies to the 111 on the right-hand side as well.

Common mistake 0⋅x=00 \cdot x = 00⋅x=0 does not mean x=0x = 0x=0

x=0x = 0x=0 is an equation with exactly one solution, zero. 0⋅x=00 \cdot x = 00⋅x=0, on the other hand, is true for all numbers, and 0⋅x=50 \cdot x = 50⋅x=5 is true for none.

#First-degree inequalities

An inequality (disequazione) is like an equation, but instead of the equals sign there is one of these symbols: >>> (greater than), ≥\geq≥ (greater than or equal to), <<< (less than), ≤\leq≤ (less than or equal to). There are usually infinitely many solutions and they form one or more intervals. Every first-degree inequality can be reduced to one of the forms ax>bax > bax>b, ax≥bax \geq bax≥b, ax<bax < bax<b, ax≤bax \leq bax≤b.

A set of solutions can be written in three equivalent ways: with an inequality, as an interval, or drawn on the number line.

InequalityIntervalMeaning
x>2x > 2x>2(2,+∞)(2, +\infty)(2,+∞)the numbers greater than 222, 222 excluded
x≥2x \geq 2x≥2[2,+∞)[2, +\infty)[2,+∞)the numbers greater than 222, 222 included
x<2x < 2x<2(−∞,2)(-\infty, 2)(−∞,2)the numbers less than 222, 222 excluded
x≤2x \leq 2x≤2(−∞,2](-\infty, 2](−∞,2]the numbers less than 222, 222 included
−1<x≤2-1 < x \leq 2−1<x≤2(−1,2](-1, 2](−1,2]between −1-1−1 (excluded) and 222 (included)

A round bracket marks an excluded endpoint, a square bracket an included endpoint. The symbol ∞\infty∞ (infinity) is not a number: next to it the bracket is always round. To put two intervals together you use the union symbol ∪\cup∪: (−∞,1)∪(3,+∞)(-\infty, 1) \cup (3, +\infty)(−∞,1)∪(3,+∞) means "x<1x < 1x<1 or x>3x > 3x>3". Sometimes "or" is written ∨\vee∨ and "and" is written ∧\wedge∧.

Rule 3.2 Equivalence principles for inequalities
  1. Adding or subtracting the same expression on both sides does not change the solutions (transposition works as in equations).
  2. Multiplying or dividing both sides by a positive number does not change the solutions.
  3. Multiplying or dividing both sides by a negative number changes the direction (verso): <<< becomes >>>, ≤\leq≤ becomes ≥\geq≥ and vice versa.

The reason for the third rule: 2<52 < 52<5 is true, but multiplying by −1-1−1 you get −2-2−2 and −5-5−5, and −2>−5-2 > -5−2>−5. Multiplying by a negative number "flips" the order of the numbers on the line.

Method Solving a first-degree inequality
  1. Remove brackets and numerical denominators (the lcm of the denominators is positive: the direction does not change).
  2. Bring the xxx terms to the left and the numbers to the right.
  3. Reach the form ax>bax > bax>b (or with one of the other three symbols).
  4. Divide by aaa: if a>0a > 0a>0 the direction stays the same, if a<0a < 0a<0 the direction is reversed.
  5. Write the solution as an inequality and as an interval; if it helps, draw it on the number line.
Example 3.4 2(x+1)−5≤4x+32(x + 1) - 5 \leq 4x + 32(x+1)−5≤4x+3

Expand: 2x+2−5≤4x+32x + 2 - 5 \leq 4x + 32x+2−5≤4x+3, that is 2x−3≤4x+32x - 3 \leq 4x + 32x−3≤4x+3.

Transpose: 2x−4x≤3+32x - 4x \leq 3 + 32x−4x≤3+3, so −2x≤6-2x \leq 6−2x≤6.

Divide by −2-2−2, which is negative, and reverse the direction: x≥−3x \geq -3x≥−3.

Solution: x≥−3x \geq -3x≥−3, that is the interval [−3,+∞)[-3, +\infty)[−3,+∞).

Example 3.5 With denominators: x3−x−12>1\frac{x}{3} - \frac{x - 1}{2} > 13x​−2x−1​>1

The lcm is 666 (positive, the direction stays the same): 2x−3(x−1)>62x - 3(x - 1) > 62x−3(x−1)>6, that is 2x−3x+3>62x - 3x + 3 > 62x−3x+3>6, so −x>3-x > 3−x>3.

Multiply by −1-1−1 and reverse: x<−3x < -3x<−3, that is the interval (−∞,−3)(-\infty, -3)(−∞,−3).

Quick check with a number that should work, x=−6x = -6x=−6: −63−−72=−2+3.5=1.5>1\frac{-6}{3} - \frac{-7}{2} = -2 + 3.5 = 1.5 > 13−6​−2−7​=−2+3.5=1.5>1. Yes.

Note When the coefficient of xxx vanishes

If after the calculations xxx disappears, you are left with an inequality between numbers. If it is true, the inequality holds for every x∈Rx \in \Rx∈R (read "xxx belonging to R\RR"); if it is false, it has no solutions. For example x+5>x+2x + 5 > x + 2x+5>x+2 becomes 0⋅x>−30 \cdot x > -30⋅x>−3, always true; x+2≥x+5x + 2 \geq x + 5x+2≥x+5 becomes 0⋅x≥30 \cdot x \geq 30⋅x≥3, never true.

Common mistake When the direction is reversed

The direction is reversed only when you multiply or divide by a negative number. Moving a term from one side to the other does not change the direction. And dividing by a positive number does not change it, even if the right-hand side is negative: from 3x<−63x < -63x<−6 it follows that x<−2x < -2x<−2.

#Several inequalities together: systems and double inequalities

A system of inequalities asks for the numbers that satisfy all the inequalities at the same time: solve each inequality and take the common part, that is the intersection (symbol ∩\cap∩). This tool will be very useful in module 4.

Example 3.6 A system of two inequalities
{2x−1>3x+4≤10\begin{cases} 2x - 1 > 3 \\ x + 4 \leq 10 \end{cases}{2x−1>3x+4≤10​

The first gives 2x>42x > 42x>4, that is x>2x > 2x>2. The second gives x≤6x \leq 6x≤6. The numbers that work for both are those with 2<x≤62 < x \leq 62<x≤6, that is the interval (2,6](2, 6](2,6].

If the two solution sets have nothing in common (for example x<1x < 1x<1 and x>3x > 3x>3) the system has no solutions.

A double inequality such as −1<2x+3≤7-1 < 2x + 3 \leq 7−1<2x+3≤7 is a system written in compact form: you can work on all three "sides" together. Subtract 333: −4<2x≤4-4 < 2x \leq 4−4<2x≤4; divide by 222: −2<x≤2-2 < x \leq 2−2<x≤2.

#First-degree word problems

Method From the text to the equation
  1. Choose the unknown and write in words what it represents (with the unit of measurement).
  2. Express all the other quantities of the problem in terms of the unknown.
  3. Translate the condition in the text into an equation, or into an inequality if the text says "at most", "at least", "no more than".
  4. Solve.
  5. Check that the result makes sense (a length is positive, a number of people is a whole number) and answer exactly the question asked.
Example 3.7 A rectangle

In a rectangle one side is three times the other and the perimeter is 484848 cm. What is the area?

Let xxx be the short side (in cm): the long side is 3x3x3x. The perimeter is the sum of the four sides: 2(x+3x)=482(x + 3x) = 482(x+3x)=48, that is 8x=488x = 488x=48 and x=6x = 6x=6. The sides are 666 cm and 181818 cm, the area is 6⋅18=1086 \cdot 18 = 1086⋅18=108 cm².

Example 3.8 Ages

Of two sisters, the older one is 333 years older than the younger one. In 555 years' time the sum of their ages will be 292929. How old are they today?

Let xxx be the age of the younger one: the older one is x+3x + 3x+3 years old. In 555 years they will be x+5x + 5x+5 and x+8x + 8x+8 years old, so (x+5)+(x+8)=29(x + 5) + (x + 8) = 29(x+5)+(x+8)=29, that is 2x+13=292x + 13 = 292x+13=29 and x=8x = 8x=8. The younger one is 888 years old, the older one 111111.

Example 3.9 A problem with an inequality

A gym charges 303030 euros to join plus 888 euros for each visit. With 100100100 euros, how many visits can you make at most?

Let nnn be the number of visits. The expense must not exceed 100100100 euros: 30+8n≤10030 + 8n \leq 10030+8n≤100, that is 8n≤708n \leq 708n≤70 and n≤8.75n \leq 8.75n≤8.75. Since nnn is a whole number, at most 8 visits.

In the test How it can appear in the test
  • Choice among four values ("the solution of ... is"): it is often quicker to substitute the options into the equation than to solve it.
  • Numeric answer: keep exact fractions until the end, simplify them and double-check the sign; with decimals and no calculator it is easy to make mistakes.
  • True/false on "impossible" and "indeterminate": bring everything to the form ax=−bax = -bax=−b and look at aaa and bbb.
  • Intervals: check the brackets (round or square) and try a number from the proposed interval in the original inequality.
  • In problems with "at most" or "at least" the result must be rounded in the right direction: n≤8.75n \leq 8.75n≤8.75 gives 888, not 999.

#3.2 Second-degree equations and inequalities

#The standard form

Definition 3.2 Second-degree equation

A second-degree (quadratic) equation in standard form (forma normale) is

ax2+bx+c=0with a≠0ax^2 + bx + c = 0 \qquad \text{with } a \neq 0ax2+bx+c=0with a=0

The numbers aaa, bbb, ccc are the coefficients; ccc is called the constant term. The solutions are also called roots and there are at most two of them, denoted by x1x_1x1​ and x2x_2x2​.

First of all you must bring the equation to standard form (everything on the left, zero on the right, like terms added up) and read the coefficients with their signs. For example:

  • 3x2−x+5=03x^2 - x + 5 = 03x2−x+5=0: a=3a = 3a=3, b=−1b = -1b=−1, c=5c = 5c=5;
  • 4−x2=04 - x^2 = 04−x2=0, that is −x2+4=0-x^2 + 4 = 0−x2+4=0: a=−1a = -1a=−1, b=0b = 0b=0, c=4c = 4c=4;
  • 2x2=7x2x^2 = 7x2x2=7x, that is 2x2−7x=02x^2 - 7x = 02x2−7x=0: a=2a = 2a=2, b=−7b = -7b=−7, c=0c = 0c=0.

#Incomplete equations

If b=0b = 0b=0 or c=0c = 0c=0 you do not need the formula: two simple ideas are enough.

Rule 3.3 Zero product property (legge di annullamento del prodotto)

A product equals zero if and only if at least one of the factors equals zero: A⋅B=0A \cdot B = 0A⋅B=0 is equivalent to A=0A = 0A=0 or B=0B = 0B=0.

TypeFormHow to solve it
pure (pura, b=0b = 0b=0)ax2+c=0ax^2 + c = 0ax2+c=0x2=−cax^2 = -\frac{c}{a}x2=−ac​: if −ca>0-\frac{c}{a} > 0−ac​>0 there are two opposite solutions x=±−cax = \pm\sqrt{-\frac{c}{a}}x=±−ac​​; if it is negative, none
spurious (spuria, c=0c = 0c=0)ax2+bx=0ax^2 + bx = 0ax2+bx=0take out the common factor: x(ax+b)=0x(ax + b) = 0x(ax+b)=0, so x=0x = 0x=0 or x=−bax = -\frac{b}{a}x=−ab​
monomial (monomia, b=c=0b = c = 0b=c=0)ax2=0ax^2 = 0ax2=0x=0x = 0x=0 (double solution)

The symbol ±\pm± is read "plus or minus" and stands for two numbers: ±3\pm 3±3 means 333 and −3-3−3.

Example 3.10 Three incomplete equations
  • 2x2−18=02x^2 - 18 = 02x2−18=0: x2=9x^2 = 9x2=9, so x=3x = 3x=3 or x=−3x = -3x=−3.
  • x2+4=0x^2 + 4 = 0x2+4=0: x2=−4x^2 = -4x2=−4, impossible in the real numbers (a square is never negative).
  • 3x2−12x=03x^2 - 12x = 03x2−12x=0: take out 3x3x3x and you get 3x(x−4)=03x(x - 4) = 03x(x−4)=0, so x=0x = 0x=0 or x=4x = 4x=4.
Common mistake Do not divide by xxx

From 3x2=12x3x^2 = 12x3x2=12x it is tempting to divide by xxx and write 3x=123x = 123x=12, that is x=4x = 4x=4. That way you lose the solution x=0x = 0x=0: bring everything to the left and take out the common factor. And from x2=9x^2 = 9x2=9 do not write only x=3x = 3x=3: (−3)2=9(-3)^2 = 9(−3)2=9 as well.

#The quadratic formula and the discriminant

Rule 3.4 Quadratic formula (formula risolutiva)

The solutions of ax2+bx+c=0ax^2 + bx + c = 0ax2+bx+c=0 are

x1,2=−b±b2−4ac2ax_{1,2} = \frac{-b \pm \sqrt{b^2 - 4ac}}{2a}x1,2​=2a−b±b2−4ac​​

The number under the root is called the discriminant and is denoted by the Greek letter Δ\DeltaΔ ("delta"): Δ=b2−4ac\Delta = b^2 - 4acΔ=b2−4ac.

  • Δ>0\Delta > 0Δ>0: two distinct real solutions, x1=−b−Δ2ax_1 = \frac{-b - \sqrt{\Delta}}{2a}x1​=2a−b−Δ​​ and x2=−b+Δ2ax_2 = \frac{-b + \sqrt{\Delta}}{2a}x2​=2a−b+Δ​​.
  • Δ=0\Delta = 0Δ=0: two coincident solutions, that is a single solution (called a double solution): x1=x2=−b2ax_1 = x_2 = -\frac{b}{2a}x1​=x2​=−2ab​.
  • Δ<0\Delta < 0Δ<0: no real solutions (the square root of a negative number is not a real number).
Method Solving a second-degree equation
  1. Bring the equation to standard form ax2+bx+c=0ax^2 + bx + c = 0ax2+bx+c=0.
  2. If it is incomplete, use the shortcuts seen above.
  3. Write down aaa, bbb, ccc with their signs.
  4. Compute Δ=b2−4ac\Delta = b^2 - 4acΔ=b2−4ac and decide how many solutions there are.
  5. If Δ≥0\Delta \geq 0Δ≥0 apply the formula and simplify the root if you can.
  6. Check with the sum and the product (you will find them further on) or by substituting.
Example 3.11 Δ>0\Delta > 0Δ>0: 2x2+x−6=02x^2 + x - 6 = 02x2+x−6=0

a=2a = 2a=2, b=1b = 1b=1, c=−6c = -6c=−6. Δ=12−4⋅2⋅(−6)=1+48=49\Delta = 1^2 - 4 \cdot 2 \cdot (-6) = 1 + 48 = 49Δ=12−4⋅2⋅(−6)=1+48=49, positive: two solutions.

x1,2=−1±492⋅2=−1±74x_{1,2} = \frac{-1 \pm \sqrt{49}}{2 \cdot 2} = \frac{-1 \pm 7}{4}x1,2​=2⋅2−1±49​​=4−1±7​

so x1=−84=−2x_1 = \frac{-8}{4} = -2x1​=4−8​=−2 and x2=64=32x_2 = \frac{6}{4} = \frac{3}{2}x2​=46​=23​.

4x2−12x+9=04x^2 - 12x + 9 = 04x2−12x+9=0: Δ=144−4⋅4⋅9=144−144=0\Delta = 144 - 4 \cdot 4 \cdot 9 = 144 - 144 = 0Δ=144−4⋅4⋅9=144−144=0. A single solution: x=−b2a=128=32x = -\frac{b}{2a} = \frac{12}{8} = \frac{3}{2}x=−2ab​=812​=23​. Indeed the trinomial is the square (2x−3)2(2x - 3)^2(2x−3)2.

Expand: 2x2+6x−(x2+2x+1)=2x+142x^2 + 6x - (x^2 + 2x + 1) = 2x + 142x2+6x−(x2+2x+1)=2x+14. The minus sign in front of the bracket changes the sign of all its terms: x2+4x−1=2x+14x^2 + 4x - 1 = 2x + 14x2+4x−1=2x+14.

(The arrow ⇒\Rightarrow⇒ is read "therefore": what is on the right follows from what is on the left.)

Rule 3.5 Reduced formula (when bbb is even)

If bbb is an even number it is easier to work with half of it, b2\frac{b}{2}2b​:

x1,2=−b2±(b2)2−acax_{1,2} = \frac{-\frac{b}{2} \pm \sqrt{\left(\frac{b}{2}\right)^2 - ac}}{a}x1,2​=a−2b​±(2b​)2−ac​​

Example 3.14 Reduced formula: x2−4x−8=0x^2 - 4x - 8 = 0x2−4x−8=0

b=−4b = -4b=−4, so b2=−2\frac{b}{2} = -22b​=−2. Under the root: (−2)2−1⋅(−8)=4+8=12(-2)^2 - 1 \cdot (-8) = 4 + 8 = 12(−2)2−1⋅(−8)=4+8=12. Then

x1,2=2±121=2±23x_{1,2} = \frac{2 \pm \sqrt{12}}{1} = 2 \pm 2\sqrt{3}x1,2​=12±12​​=2±23​

because 12=4⋅3=23\sqrt{12} = \sqrt{4 \cdot 3} = 2\sqrt{3}12​=4⋅3​=23​. With the full formula: Δ=16+32=48\Delta = 16 + 32 = 48Δ=16+32=48 and 4±482=4±432=2±23\frac{4 \pm \sqrt{48}}{2} = \frac{4 \pm 4\sqrt{3}}{2} = 2 \pm 2\sqrt{3}24±48​​=24±43​​=2±23​. Same result, longer calculations.

#Where the formula comes from

The formula is obtained by completing the square: you add to both sides the number that turns the part with xxx into the square of a binomial. First look at a case with numbers, x2+6x+5=0x^2 + 6x + 5 = 0x2+6x+5=0:

  • bring the constant term to the right: x2+6x=−5x^2 + 6x = -5x2+6x=−5;
  • take half the coefficient of xxx, that is 333, and its square, 999; add it to both sides: x2+6x+9=4x^2 + 6x + 9 = 4x2+6x+9=4;
  • on the left there is a square: (x+3)2=4(x + 3)^2 = 4(x+3)2=4;
  • so x+3=2x + 3 = 2x+3=2 or x+3=−2x + 3 = -2x+3=−2, that is x=−1x = -1x=−1 or x=−5x = -5x=−5.

In the general case you do the same, after dividing everything by aaa (half the coefficient of xxx is b2a\frac{b}{2a}2ab​, and its square is b24a2\frac{b^2}{4a^2}4a2b2​):

x2+bax+ca=0x2+bax=−cax2+bax+b24a2=b24a2−ca(x+b2a)2=b2−4ac4a2\begin{aligned} x^2 + \frac{b}{a}x + \frac{c}{a} &= 0 \\ x^2 + \frac{b}{a}x &= -\frac{c}{a} \\ x^2 + \frac{b}{a}x + \frac{b^2}{4a^2} &= \frac{b^2}{4a^2} - \frac{c}{a} \\ \left(x + \frac{b}{2a}\right)^2 &= \frac{b^2 - 4ac}{4a^2} \end{aligned}x2+ab​x+ac​x2+ab​xx2+ab​x+4a2b2​(x+2ab​)2​=0=−ac​=4a2b2​−ac​=4a2b2−4ac​​

If the right-hand side is positive or zero you can take the square root of both sides, with the ±\pm±:

x+b2a=±b2−4ac2ax + \frac{b}{2a} = \pm\frac{\sqrt{b^2 - 4ac}}{2a}x+2ab​=±2ab2−4ac​​

Isolating xxx you find the quadratic formula. You can also see why the sign of Δ=b2−4ac\Delta = b^2 - 4acΔ=b2−4ac matters: the left-hand side is a square and cannot be negative, while the right-hand side has the same sign as Δ\DeltaΔ (the denominator 4a24a^24a2 is positive). If Δ<0\Delta < 0Δ<0 the equality is impossible.

#Factorisation, sum and product of the roots

Rule 3.6 Factorising the second-degree trinomial

If Δ≥0\Delta \geq 0Δ≥0 and x1x_1x1​, x2x_2x2​ are the solutions of ax2+bx+c=0ax^2 + bx + c = 0ax2+bx+c=0, then

ax2+bx+c=a(x−x1)(x−x2)ax^2 + bx + c = a(x - x_1)(x - x_2)ax2+bx+c=a(x−x1​)(x−x2​)

If Δ<0\Delta < 0Δ<0 the trinomial cannot be factorised over the real numbers.

Expanding the product you find two very useful relations:

x1+x2=−bax1⋅x2=cax_1 + x_2 = -\frac{b}{a} \qquad\qquad x_1 \cdot x_2 = \frac{c}{a}x1​+x2​=−ab​x1​⋅x2​=ac​

This rule generalises the quadratic trinomial (sum and product method) of module 2, x2+sx+p=(x+A)(x+B)x^2 + sx + p = (x + A)(x + B)x2+sx+p=(x+A)(x+B) when A+B=sA + B = sA+B=s and A⋅B=pA \cdot B = pA⋅B=p. Now you can factorise any second-degree trinomial with Δ≥0\Delta \geq 0Δ≥0, even when you cannot guess the two numbers.

Example 3.15 Factorising 2x2+x−62x^2 + x - 62x2+x−6

The roots are −2-2−2 and 32\frac{3}{2}23​ (from the earlier example). So

2x2+x−6=2(x+2)(x−32)=(x+2)(2x−3)2x^2 + x - 6 = 2(x + 2)\left(x - \frac{3}{2}\right) = (x + 2)(2x - 3)2x2+x−6=2(x+2)(x−23​)=(x+2)(2x−3)

where the 222 has gone into the last bracket. Check: (x+2)(2x−3)=2x2−3x+4x−6=2x2+x−6(x + 2)(2x - 3) = 2x^2 - 3x + 4x - 6 = 2x^2 + x - 6(x+2)(2x−3)=2x2−3x+4x−6=2x2+x−6.

Example 3.16 Two numbers with a given sum and product

Which numbers have sum 777 and product 101010? They are the solutions of t2−7t+10=0t^2 - 7t + 10 = 0t2−7t+10=0 (in this equation the sum of the roots is 777 and the product is 101010). Δ=49−40=9\Delta = 49 - 40 = 9Δ=49−40=9, t=7±32t = \frac{7 \pm 3}{2}t=27±3​: the numbers are 555 and 222.

Common mistake Do not forget aaa

2x2+x−62x^2 + x - 62x2+x−6 is not (x+2)(x−32)(x + 2)\left(x - \frac{3}{2}\right)(x+2)(x−23​): that product equals x2+12x−3x^2 + \frac{1}{2}x - 3x2+21​x−3, that is half of it. The coefficient aaa always goes in front.

In the test Quick checks without a calculator
  • "What are the solutions of x2−x−12=0x^2 - x - 12 = 0x2−x−12=0?": look for two numbers with sum 111 and product −12-12−12, that is 444 and −3-3−3. This is often enough to choose the right option without computing Δ\DeltaΔ.
  • "How many real solutions does ... have": you only need the sign of Δ\DeltaΔ. If aaa and ccc have opposite signs, −4ac-4ac−4ac is positive and so Δ>0\Delta > 0Δ>0 for sure.
  • With integer coefficients, if Δ\DeltaΔ is a perfect square (1,4,9,16,25,…1, 4, 9, 16, 25, \ldots1,4,9,16,25,…) the solutions are fractions or integers; if Δ\DeltaΔ is positive but not a perfect square, radicals appear, and the options with only integers are wrong.
  • Questions with a parameter ("for which kkk are there two coincident solutions?"): set Δ=0\Delta = 0Δ=0 (or Δ>0\Delta > 0Δ>0, Δ<0\Delta < 0Δ<0) and solve for kkk.

#Second-degree inequalities with the parabola

A second-degree inequality can be reduced to one of the forms ax2+bx+c>0ax^2 + bx + c > 0ax2+bx+c>0, ≥0\geq 0≥0, <0< 0<0, ≤0\leq 0≤0, with a≠0a \neq 0a=0. The safest way to solve it is to think of the graph of y=ax2+bx+cy = ax^2 + bx + cy=ax2+bx+c, which is a parabola (you will study it in module 5):

  • if a>0a > 0a>0 the parabola is concave up (it "opens upwards"), if a<0a < 0a<0 it is concave down;
  • the points where it crosses the xxx-axis are the solutions of the associated equation ax2+bx+c=0ax^2 + bx + c = 0ax2+bx+c=0;
  • the trinomial is positive where the parabola lies above the xxx-axis and negative where it lies below it.
Rule 3.7 Sign of ax2+bx+cax^2 + bx + cax2+bx+c when a>0a > 0a>0

Let x1<x2x_1 < x_2x1​<x2​ be the solutions of the associated equation when Δ>0\Delta > 0Δ>0, and x0=−b2ax_0 = -\frac{b}{2a}x0​=−2ab​ the double solution when Δ=0\Delta = 0Δ=0.

DirectionΔ>0\Delta > 0Δ>0Δ=0\Delta = 0Δ=0Δ<0\Delta < 0Δ<0
>0> 0>0x<x1x < x_1x<x1​ or x>x2x > x_2x>x2​every x≠x0x \neq x_0x=x0​every x∈Rx \in \Rx∈R

≤0\leq 0≤0x1≤x≤x2x_1 \leq x \leq x_2x1​≤x≤x2​only x=x0x = x_0x=x0​no solutions

In short, with Δ>0\Delta > 0Δ>0: direction >>> → outer intervals, direction <<< → inner interval. If a<0a < 0a<0 multiply everything by −1-1−1, reverse the direction and then use the table.

Method Solving a second-degree inequality
  1. Bring the inequality to standard form: trinomial on the left, 000 on the right.
  2. If a<0a < 0a<0, multiply by −1-1−1 and reverse the direction.
  3. Solve the associated equation: find x1x_1x1​ and x2x_2x2​, or find out that Δ≤0\Delta \leq 0Δ≤0.
  4. Sketch by hand an upward-opening parabola through the roots and choose where it lies above the axis (direction >>>) or below it (direction <<<).
  5. With ≥\geq≥ or ≤\leq≤ include the roots, with >>> or <<< exclude them.
Example 3.17 x2−2x−3>0x^2 - 2x - 3 > 0x2−2x−3>0

Associated equation: x2−2x−3=0x^2 - 2x - 3 = 0x2−2x−3=0, with Δ=4+12=16\Delta = 4 + 12 = 16Δ=4+12=16 and x=2±42x = \frac{2 \pm 4}{2}x=22±4​, that is x1=−1x_1 = -1x1​=−1 and x2=3x_2 = 3x2​=3. Solution: x<−1x < -1x<−1 or x>3x > 3x>3, that is (−∞,−1)∪(3,+∞)(-\infty, -1) \cup (3, +\infty)(−∞,−1)∪(3,+∞).

Multiply by −1-1−1 and reverse: 2x2−5x−3≤02x^2 - 5x - 3 \leq 02x2−5x−3≤0. Δ=25+24=49\Delta = 25 + 24 = 49Δ=25+24=49, x=5±74x = \frac{5 \pm 7}{4}x=45±7​: x1=−12x_1 = -\frac{1}{2}x1​=−21​ and x2=3x_2 = 3x2​=3. Direction ≤\leq≤: inner interval, endpoints included. Solution: −12≤x≤3-\frac{1}{2} \leq x \leq 3−21​≤x≤3, that is [−12,3]\left[-\frac{1}{2}, 3\right][−21​,3].

Example 3.19 Δ=0\Delta = 0Δ=0 and Δ<0\Delta < 0Δ<0

x2+4x+4>0x^2 + 4x + 4 > 0x2+4x+4>0: the trinomial is the square (x+2)2(x + 2)^2(x+2)2, which is zero only for x=−2x = -2x=−2 and positive elsewhere. Solution: x≠−2x \neq -2x=−2. With the direction ≤0\leq 0≤0, on the other hand, the only solution would be x=−2x = -2x=−2.

x2+x+1<0x^2 + x + 1 < 0x2+x+1<0: Δ=1−4=−3<0\Delta = 1 - 4 = -3 < 0Δ=1−4=−3<0 and the parabola lies entirely above the axis. No solutions. With the direction >0> 0>0 the solution would be every x∈Rx \in \Rx∈R.

And x2>−4x^2 > -4x2>−4 is true for every xxx, because a square is never negative. Another common mistake: multiplying by −1-1−1 to make aaa positive and forgetting to reverse the direction.

In the test Discarding options quickly

When the answers are four sets, try a convenient number (often x=0x = 0x=0) in the original inequality. For x2−2x−3>0x^2 - 2x - 3 > 0x2−2x−3>0, with x=0x = 0x=0 you get −3>0-3 > 0−3>0, false: all the options that contain 000 are wrong. Then check the endpoints: they are included only if the direction is ≥\geq≥ or ≤\leq≤.

#Second-degree word problems

The method is the same as for first-degree problems, but you often find two solutions and one of them may not be acceptable (a negative length, a negative age, a non-integer number of objects).

Example 3.20 The sides of a rectangle

A rectangle has area 606060 cm² and one side is 777 cm longer than the other. Let xxx be the short side: the other one is x+7x + 7x+7 and x(x+7)=60x(x + 7) = 60x(x+7)=60, that is x2+7x−60=0x^2 + 7x - 60 = 0x2+7x−60=0. Δ=49+240=289=172\Delta = 49 + 240 = 289 = 17^2Δ=49+240=289=172, so x=−7±172x = \frac{-7 \pm 17}{2}x=2−7±17​: x=5x = 5x=5 or x=−12x = -12x=−12. A length cannot be negative: the sides are 555 cm and 121212 cm.

Example 3.21 Consecutive numbers

The product of two consecutive natural numbers is 132132132. With xxx the smaller one: x(x+1)=132x(x + 1) = 132x(x+1)=132, that is x2+x−132=0x^2 + x - 132 = 0x2+x−132=0. Δ=1+528=529=232\Delta = 1 + 528 = 529 = 23^2Δ=1+528=529=232, x=−1±232x = \frac{-1 \pm 23}{2}x=2−1±23​: x=11x = 11x=11 or x=−12x = -12x=−12. Natural numbers are not negative: the numbers you are looking for are 111111 and 121212.

Example 3.22 A stone thrown upwards

The height (in metres) of a stone after ttt seconds is h=20t−5t2h = 20t - 5t^2h=20t−5t2. When is it at 151515 m? And for how long does it stay above 151515 m?

20t−5t2=1520t - 5t^2 = 1520t−5t2=15 becomes 5t2−20t+15=05t^2 - 20t + 15 = 05t2−20t+15=0, that is, dividing by 555, t2−4t+3=0t^2 - 4t + 3 = 0t2−4t+3=0: t=1t = 1t=1 or t=3t = 3t=3. The stone passes 151515 m on the way up after 111 second and on the way down after 333 seconds.

Above 151515 m: 20t−5t2>1520t - 5t^2 > 1520t−5t2>15, that is −5t2+20t−15>0-5t^2 + 20t - 15 > 0−5t2+20t−15>0; dividing by −5-5−5 the direction is reversed: t2−4t+3<0t^2 - 4t + 3 < 0t2−4t+3<0, which holds for 1<t<31 < t < 31<t<3. The stone stays above 151515 m for 222 seconds.

#3.3 Systems of equations

#What a system is

Definition 3.3 System and solution

A system is a group of two or more equations that must hold at the same time. It is written with a curly bracket:

{x+y=5x−y=1\begin{cases} x + y = 5 \\ x - y = 1 \end{cases}{x+y=5x−y=1​

A solution of a system in two unknowns is an ordered pair (x,y)(x, y)(x,y) that makes all the equations true; with three unknowns it is a triple (x,y,z)(x, y, z)(x,y,z), and so on. Here the solution is (3,2)(3, 2)(3,2): 3+2=53 + 2 = 53+2=5 and 3−2=13 - 2 = 13−2=1. The pair (2,3)(2, 3)(2,3), on the other hand, does not work, because the order matters.

A system can have:

  • a single solution (in systems of degree higher than one, possibly more than one, but finitely many): it is called determined;
  • infinitely many solutions: it is called indeterminate;
  • no solutions: it is called impossible or inconsistent.

In the first two cases the system is consistent.

Definition 3.4 Degree of a system

The degree of a polynomial equation in several unknowns is the highest degree of its terms; in a term such as x2yx^2yx2y you add the exponents (2+1=32 + 1 = 32+1=3). The degree of a system is the product of the degrees of its equations. For example:

{x+y=3xy=2 has degree 1⋅2=2,{x3−y=0x2+y2=1 has degree 3⋅2=6.\begin{cases} x + y = 3 \\ xy = 2 \end{cases} \text{ has degree } 1 \cdot 2 = 2, \qquad \begin{cases} x^3 - y = 0 \\ x^2 + y^2 = 1 \end{cases} \text{ has degree } 3 \cdot 2 = 6.{x+y=3xy=2​ has degree 1⋅2=2,{x3−y=0x2+y2=1​ has degree 3⋅2=6.

A system of degree 111, made only of first-degree equations, is called a linear system. With two equations and two unknowns its standard form is

{a1x+b1y=c1a2x+b2y=c2\begin{cases} a_1 x + b_1 y = c_1 \\ a_2 x + b_2 y = c_2 \end{cases}{a1​x+b1​y=c1​a2​x+b2​y=c2​​

where a1,b1,c1,a2,b2,c2a_1, b_1, c_1, a_2, b_2, c_2a1​,b1​,c1​,a2​,b2​,c2​ are real numbers. If the constant terms c1c_1c1​ and c2c_2c2​ are both zero the system is called homogeneous, and it always has at least the solution (0,0)(0, 0)(0,0), called the zero solution.

#Substitution method

Method Substitution
  1. From one of the equations, express one unknown in terms of the other (choose the one with coefficient 111 or −1-1−1: no fractions).
  2. Substitute the expression you found into the other equation: you get an equation with only one unknown.
  3. Solve it.
  4. Put the value you found into the expression from step 1 and compute the other unknown.
  5. Write the pair (x,y)(x, y)(x,y) and check it in both equations.
Example 3.23 Substitution
{2x+y=73x−2y=7\begin{cases} 2x + y = 7 \\ 3x - 2y = 7 \end{cases}{2x+y=73x−2y=7​

From the first: y=7−2xy = 7 - 2xy=7−2x. Substitute into the second: 3x−2(7−2x)=73x - 2(7 - 2x) = 73x−2(7−2x)=7, that is 3x−14+4x=73x - 14 + 4x = 73x−14+4x=7, so 7x=217x = 217x=21 and x=3x = 3x=3. Then y=7−2⋅3=1y = 7 - 2 \cdot 3 = 1y=7−2⋅3=1.

Solution: (3,1)(3, 1)(3,1). Check: 6+1=76 + 1 = 76+1=7 and 9−2=79 - 2 = 79−2=7.

#Comparison method

It is a variant of substitution: you express the same unknown from both equations and then set the two expressions equal.

Example 3.24 Comparison
{y=2x−1y=−x+5\begin{cases} y = 2x - 1 \\ y = -x + 5 \end{cases}{y=2x−1y=−x+5​

The two expressions for yyy must be equal: 2x−1=−x+52x - 1 = -x + 52x−1=−x+5, so 3x=63x = 63x=6 and x=2x = 2x=2. Then y=2⋅2−1=3y = 2 \cdot 2 - 1 = 3y=2⋅2−1=3. Solution: (2,3)(2, 3)(2,3).

Every linear equation in xxx and yyy represents a straight line in the Cartesian plane (module 5): solving the system means finding the point where the two lines meet.

#Elimination method

Method Elimination (riduzione, also called Gauss's method)
  1. Multiply one or both equations by non-zero numbers so that one of the unknowns has opposite (or equal) coefficients in the two equations.
  2. Add the two equations side by side (or subtract them, if the coefficients are equal): that unknown disappears.
  3. Solve the remaining equation in one unknown.
  4. Substitute the value you found into one of the original equations and find the other unknown.

The equation obtained by adding can replace one of the two original equations: the new system is equivalent, that is it has the same solutions.

Example 3.25 Coefficients already opposite
{3x+2y=125x−2y=4\begin{cases} 3x + 2y = 12 \\ 5x - 2y = 4 \end{cases}{3x+2y=125x−2y=4​

The coefficients of yyy are 222 and −2-2−2: adding side by side you get 8x=168x = 168x=16, so x=2x = 2x=2. From the first: 6+2y=126 + 2y = 126+2y=12, that is y=3y = 3y=3. Solution: (2,3)(2, 3)(2,3).

Example 3.26 Multiply first
{2x+3y=13x+4y=2\begin{cases} 2x + 3y = 1 \\ 3x + 4y = 2 \end{cases}{2x+3y=13x+4y=2​

Multiply the first by 333 and the second by 222: 6x+9y=36x + 9y = 36x+9y=3 and 6x+8y=46x + 8y = 46x+8y=4. Subtract the second from the first: y=−1y = -1y=−1. Then 2x−3=12x - 3 = 12x−3=1, so x=2x = 2x=2. Solution: (2,−1)(2, -1)(2,−1).

Common mistake Multiply all the terms

When you multiply an equation by a number, multiply the constant term too. And watch the signs when you subtract: (6x+9y)−(6x+8y)=y(6x + 9y) - (6x + 8y) = y(6x+9y)−(6x+8y)=y, but on the right 3−4=−13 - 4 = -13−4=−1.

Note Cramer's rule

For the system a1x+b1y=c1a_1x + b_1y = c_1a1​x+b1​y=c1​, a2x+b2y=c2a_2x + b_2y = c_2a2​x+b2​y=c2​ compute the number D=a1b2−a2b1D = a_1b_2 - a_2b_1D=a1​b2​−a2​b1​. If D≠0D \neq 0D=0 the solution is unique and it is

x=c1b2−c2b1Dy=a1c2−a2c1Dx = \frac{c_1b_2 - c_2b_1}{D} \qquad y = \frac{a_1c_2 - a_2c_1}{D}x=Dc1​b2​−c2​b1​​y=Da1​c2​−a2​c1​​

In the previous example: D=2⋅4−3⋅3=−1D = 2 \cdot 4 - 3 \cdot 3 = -1D=2⋅4−3⋅3=−1, x=1⋅4−2⋅3−1=2x = \frac{1 \cdot 4 - 2 \cdot 3}{-1} = 2x=−11⋅4−2⋅3​=2, y=2⋅2−3⋅1−1=−1y = \frac{2 \cdot 2 - 3 \cdot 1}{-1} = -1y=−12⋅2−3⋅1​=−1. It is handy for checking a result. If D=0D = 0D=0 the system is impossible or indeterminate.

#How many solutions a linear system has

If, while solving a system, the unknowns all disappear together, you are left with an equality between numbers:

  • if it is false (for example 0=10 = 10=1) the system is impossible;
  • if it is true (0=00 = 00=0) the system is indeterminate: one of the equations adds no information.
Rule 3.8 Comparing the coefficients

For the system a1x+b1y=c1a_1 x + b_1 y = c_1a1​x+b1​y=c1​, a2x+b2y=c2a_2 x + b_2 y = c_2a2​x+b2​y=c2​, with non-zero coefficients:

ConditionSystemLines
a1a2≠b1b2\frac{a_1}{a_2} \neq \frac{b_1}{b_2}a2​a1​​=b2​b1​​determined (one solution)intersecting
a1a2=b1b2≠c1c2\frac{a_1}{a_2} = \frac{b_1}{b_2} \neq \frac{c_1}{c_2}a2​a1​​=b2​b1​​=c2​c1​​impossibleparallel and distinct
a1a2=b1b2=c1c2\frac{a_1}{a_2} = \frac{b_1}{b_2} = \frac{c_1}{c_2}a2​a1​​=b2​b1​​=c2​c1​​indeterminatecoincident
Example 3.27 An impossible system
{x+2y=32x+4y=5\begin{cases} x + 2y = 3 \\ 2x + 4y = 5 \end{cases}{x+2y=32x+4y=5​

Multiply the first by 222: 2x+4y=62x + 4y = 62x+4y=6. But the second says 2x+4y=52x + 4y = 52x+4y=5: subtracting you get 0=10 = 10=1, false. The system is impossible: the two lines are parallel. With the ratios: 12=24\frac{1}{2} = \frac{2}{4}21​=42​, but 35\frac{3}{5}53​ is different.

Example 3.28 An indeterminate system
{x−y=23x−3y=6\begin{cases} x - y = 2 \\ 3x - 3y = 6 \end{cases}{x−y=23x−3y=6​

The second equation is the first multiplied by 333: they represent the same line. Every pair with x−y=2x - y = 2x−y=2 works: setting y=ty = ty=t, where ttt is any real number (a parameter), the solutions are the pairs (2+t,t)(2 + t, t)(2+t,t). For example (2,0)(2, 0)(2,0), (3,1)(3, 1)(3,1), (0,−2)(0, -2)(0,−2).

#Systems with three unknowns

With three equations in three unknowns you use the same methods: with a substitution (or an elimination) you remove one unknown and reduce the problem to a system of two equations in two unknowns.

Example 3.29 A system of three equations in three unknowns
{x+y+z=6x−y=−1y+2z=8\begin{cases} x + y + z = 6 \\ x - y = -1 \\ y + 2z = 8 \end{cases}⎩⎨⎧​x+y+z=6x−y=−1y+2z=8​

From the second: x=y−1x = y - 1x=y−1. Substitute into the first: (y−1)+y+z=6(y - 1) + y + z = 6(y−1)+y+z=6, that is 2y+z=72y + z = 72y+z=7. Now you have a system in yyy and zzz:

{2y+z=7y+2z=8\begin{cases} 2y + z = 7 \\ y + 2z = 8 \end{cases}{2y+z=7y+2z=8​

From the first z=7−2yz = 7 - 2yz=7−2y; in the second y+14−4y=8y + 14 - 4y = 8y+14−4y=8, so −3y=−6-3y = -6−3y=−6 and y=2y = 2y=2. Then z=3z = 3z=3 and x=1x = 1x=1. Solution: the triple (1,2,3)(1, 2, 3)(1,2,3).

With three unknowns too, a system can be impossible (at some point you find a false equality, such as 0=−20 = -20=−2) or indeterminate: in that case the solutions are written in terms of a parameter, as in the indeterminate system seen above.

#Higher-degree systems (an outline)

Sum and product system. The system

{x+y=sxy=p\begin{cases} x + y = s \\ xy = p \end{cases}{x+y=sxy=p​

has degree 222. The numbers xxx and yyy are the solutions of the equation t2−st+p=0t^2 - st + p = 0t2−st+p=0 (it is the same idea as the sum and product of the roots). It is the system you solve without noticing when you factorise x2+sx+px^2 + sx + px2+sx+p by looking for two numbers with sum sss and product ppp.

Example 3.30 Sum 555 and product 666

t2−5t+6=0t^2 - 5t + 6 = 0t2−5t+6=0 has solutions t=2t = 2t=2 and t=3t = 3t=3. The system x+y=5x + y = 5x+y=5, xy=6xy = 6xy=6 therefore has two solutions: (2,3)(2, 3)(2,3) and (3,2)(3, 2)(3,2).

A second-degree equation and a first-degree one. You use substitution: express one unknown from the first-degree equation and substitute it into the second-degree one.

Example 3.31 Circle and line
{x2+y2=10x−y=2\begin{cases} x^2 + y^2 = 10 \\ x - y = 2 \end{cases}{x2+y2=10x−y=2​

From the second x=y+2x = y + 2x=y+2. In the first: (y+2)2+y2=10(y + 2)^2 + y^2 = 10(y+2)2+y2=10, that is 2y2+4y−6=02y^2 + 4y - 6 = 02y2+4y−6=0 and, dividing by 222, y2+2y−3=0y^2 + 2y - 3 = 0y2+2y−3=0, with solutions y=1y = 1y=1 and y=−3y = -3y=−3. From x=y+2x = y + 2x=y+2: if y=1y = 1y=1 then x=3x = 3x=3; if y=−3y = -3y=−3 then x=−1x = -1x=−1. Solutions: (3,1)(3, 1)(3,1) and (−1,−3)(-1, -3)(−1,−3).

A linear system has at most one solution (if it is not indeterminate); a second-degree system like this one can have two. For higher degrees the calculations quickly become very complicated.

#Word problems with systems

When a problem has two unknown quantities it is often more natural to use two unknowns and a system.

Example 3.32 A two-digit number

In a two-digit number the sum of the digits is 999; swapping the digits gives a number that is 272727 greater than the original one. What is the number?

Let ddd be the tens digit and uuu the units digit: the number is 10d+u10d + u10d+u and the one with the digits swapped is 10u+d10u + d10u+d. Then

{d+u=9(10u+d)−(10d+u)=27\begin{cases} d + u = 9 \\ (10u + d) - (10d + u) = 27 \end{cases}{d+u=9(10u+d)−(10d+u)=27​

The second becomes 9u−9d=279u - 9d = 279u−9d=27, that is u−d=3u - d = 3u−d=3. Adding it to the first: 2u=122u = 122u=12, so u=6u = 6u=6 and d=3d = 3d=3. The number is 363636 (indeed 63−36=2763 - 36 = 2763−36=27).

Example 3.33 Notebooks and pens

333 notebooks and 222 pens cost 999 euros; 111 notebook and 444 pens cost 888 euros. With qqq the price of a notebook and ppp that of a pen:

{3q+2p=9q+4p=8\begin{cases} 3q + 2p = 9 \\ q + 4p = 8 \end{cases}{3q+2p=9q+4p=8​

From the second q=8−4pq = 8 - 4pq=8−4p; in the first 24−12p+2p=924 - 12p + 2p = 924−12p+2p=9, that is −10p=−15-10p = -15−10p=−15 and p=1.5p = 1.5p=1.5. Then q=8−6=2q = 8 - 6 = 2q=8−6=2. A notebook costs 222 euros, a pen 1.501.501.50 euros.

In the test Systems in the test
  • "Which pair is a solution of the system?": substitute the proposed pairs into both equations. The typical distractors satisfy only one equation or have xxx and yyy swapped.
  • "Is the system determined, impossible or indeterminate?": compare the ratios of the coefficients, without solving.
  • "What is the degree of the system?": multiply the degrees of the equations, do not add them.
  • With a parameter ("for which value of kkk is the system impossible?"): require the ratios of the coefficients of xxx and of yyy to be equal and check that the ratio of the constant terms is different.

#Exercises

Exercise 3.1BasicAn equation with brackets

Solve 5x−2(x+3)=x+45x - 2(x + 3) = x + 45x−2(x+3)=x+4.

Solution

Expand the product: 5x−2x−6=x+45x - 2x - 6 = x + 45x−2x−6=x+4, that is 3x−6=x+43x - 6 = x + 43x−6=x+4.

Transpose: 3x−x=4+63x - x = 4 + 63x−x=4+6, so 2x=102x = 102x=10 and x=5x = 5x=5.

Check: on the left 25−2⋅8=925 - 2 \cdot 8 = 925−2⋅8=9, on the right 5+4=95 + 4 = 95+4=9.

Exercise 3.2BasicWhat type of equation?

Decide whether each equation is determined, impossible or indeterminate, and solve the determined one.

  1. 3(x−2)=3x−63(x - 2) = 3x - 63(x−2)=3x−6
  2. 2x+1=2(x+1)2x + 1 = 2(x + 1)2x+1=2(x+1)
  3. 4x−3=x+34x - 3 = x + 34x−3=x+3
Solution
  1. 3x−6=3x−63x - 6 = 3x - 63x−6=3x−6, that is 0⋅x=00 \cdot x = 00⋅x=0: indeterminate (identity), every x∈Rx \in \Rx∈R is a solution.
  2. 2x+1=2x+22x + 1 = 2x + 22x+1=2x+2, that is 0⋅x=10 \cdot x = 10⋅x=1: impossible.
  3. 4x−x=3+34x - x = 3 + 34x−x=3+3, that is 3x=63x = 63x=6: determined, with solution x=2x = 2x=2.

  2. Solve the system formed by 3−2x≥x−93 - 2x \geq x - 93−2x≥x−9 and 2x+1>02x + 1 > 02x+1>0.

  2. The second inequality gives 2x>−12x > -12x>−1, that is x>−12x > -\frac{1}{2}x>−21​. The common part with x≤4x \leq 4x≤4 is −12<x≤4-\frac{1}{2} < x \leq 4−21​<x≤4, that is (−12,4]\left(-\frac{1}{2}, 4\right](−21​,4].

Exercise 3.5BasicA linear system

Solve by substitution:

{x+3y=52x−y=3\begin{cases} x + 3y = 5 \\ 2x - y = 3 \end{cases}{x+3y=52x−y=3​
Solution

From the first x=5−3yx = 5 - 3yx=5−3y. In the second: 2(5−3y)−y=32(5 - 3y) - y = 32(5−3y)−y=3, that is 10−6y−y=310 - 6y - y = 310−6y−y=3, so −7y=−7-7y = -7−7y=−7 and y=1y = 1y=1. Then x=5−3=2x = 5 - 3 = 2x=5−3=2.

Exercise 3.6IntermediateAn equation with denominators

Solve 2x−13−x+24=x6−1\frac{2x - 1}{3} - \frac{x + 2}{4} = \frac{x}{6} - 132x−1​−4x+2​=6x​−1.

Solution

The lcm of 333, 444 and 666 is 121212. Multiply every term by 121212, including the −1-1−1:

4(2x−1)−3(x+2)=2x−124(2x - 1) - 3(x + 2) = 2x - 124(2x−1)−3(x+2)=2x−12

Expand: 8x−4−3x−6=2x−128x - 4 - 3x - 6 = 2x - 128x−4−3x−6=2x−12, that is 5x−10=2x−125x - 10 = 2x - 125x−10=2x−12. Transpose: 3x=−23x = -23x=−2, so x=−23x = -\frac{2}{3}x=−32​.

Check: on the left −7/33−4/34=−79−39=−109\frac{-7/3}{3} - \frac{4/3}{4} = -\frac{7}{9} - \frac{3}{9} = -\frac{10}{9}3−7/3​−44/3​=−97​−93​=−910​; on the right −19−1=−109-\frac{1}{9} - 1 = -\frac{10}{9}−91​−1=−910​.

Solve:

Exercise 3.9IntermediateA group of friends

A third of a group of friends goes to the cinema, a quarter goes to the theatre and the remaining 101010 stay at home. How many people are there in the group?

Solution

Let xxx be the number of people. x3\frac{x}{3}3x​ go to the cinema, x4\frac{x}{4}4x​ to the theatre, 101010 stay at home, and altogether there are xxx of them:

x3+x4+10=x\frac{x}{3} + \frac{x}{4} + 10 = x3x​+4x​+10=x

Multiply by 121212: 4x+3x+120=12x4x + 3x + 120 = 12x4x+3x+120=12x, so 120=5x120 = 5x120=5x and x=24x = 24x=24. Check: 888 at the cinema, 666 at the theatre, 101010 at home, and 8+6+10=248 + 6 + 10 = 248+6+10=24.

Exercise 3.10IntermediateA rectangular vegetable garden

A rectangular vegetable garden has perimeter 262626 m and area 404040 m². How long are the sides?

Solution

If xxx and yyy are the sides, 2(x+y)=262(x + y) = 262(x+y)=26 and xy=40xy = 40xy=40, that is

{x+y=13xy=40\begin{cases} x + y = 13 \\ xy = 40 \end{cases}{x+y=13xy=40​

It is a sum and product system: xxx and yyy are the solutions of t2−13t+40=0t^2 - 13t + 40 = 0t2−13t+40=0. Δ=169−160=9\Delta = 169 - 160 = 9Δ=169−160=9, t=13±32t = \frac{13 \pm 3}{2}t=213±3​: t=8t = 8t=8 or t=5t = 5t=5. The sides are 555 m and 888 m long.

Exercise 3.11IntermediateA system with three unknowns

Solve

{x+y−z=12x+y=3x+z=2\begin{cases} x + y - z = 1 \\ 2x + y = 3 \\ x + z = 2 \end{cases}⎩⎨⎧​x+y−z=12x+y=3x+z=2​
Solution

From the third z=2−xz = 2 - xz=2−x. In the first: x+y−(2−x)=1x + y - (2 - x) = 1x+y−(2−x)=1, that is 2x+y=32x + y = 32x+y=3: it is the same equation as the second. Only two different equations remain for three unknowns: the system is indeterminate.

Set x=tx = tx=t (parameter): from the second y=3−2ty = 3 - 2ty=3−2t, from the third z=2−tz = 2 - tz=2−t. The solutions are the triples (t,3−2t,2−t)(t, 3 - 2t, 2 - t)(t,3−2t,2−t) with t∈Rt \in \Rt∈R; for example with t=0t = 0t=0 you get (0,3,2)(0, 3, 2)(0,3,2) and with t=1t = 1t=1 you get (1,1,1)(1, 1, 1)(1,1,1).

Exercise 3.12Test levelAn equation with a parameter

Consider the equation (k−2)x=k+1(k - 2)x = k + 1(k−2)x=k+1, where kkk is a real number.

  1. For which value of kkk is it impossible?
  2. Is there a value of kkk for which it is indeterminate?
  3. For k=5k = 5k=5, what is the solution?
Solution
  1. It is impossible when the coefficient of xxx is zero and the constant term is not: k−2=0k - 2 = 0k−2=0, that is k=2k = 2k=2. Then it becomes 0⋅x=30 \cdot x = 30⋅x=3, false for every xxx.
  2. You would need both k−2=0k - 2 = 0k−2=0 and k+1=0k + 1 = 0k+1=0, that is k=2k = 2k=2 and k=−1k = -1k=−1: this cannot happen. No value of kkk makes it indeterminate.
  3. With k=5k = 5k=5: 3x=63x = 63x=6, so x=2x = 2x=2.

For which values of kkk does the equation x2−6x+k=0x^2 - 6x + k = 0x2−6x+k=0 have two distinct real solutions? For which value does it have only one, and what is it?

Δ=36−4k\Delta = 36 - 4kΔ=36−4k. Two distinct solutions if 36−4k>036 - 4k > 036−4k>0, that is k<9k < 9k<9. A single solution if Δ=0\Delta = 0Δ=0, that is k=9k = 9k=9: the equation becomes x2−6x+9=(x−3)2=0x^2 - 6x + 9 = (x - 3)^2 = 0x2−6x+9=(x−3)2=0 and the solution is x=3x = 3x=3. For k>9k > 9k>9 there are no real solutions.

Without solving the equation 2x2−7x+3=02x^2 - 7x + 3 = 02x2−7x+3=0, compute the sum and the product of the solutions. Then find the solutions and check.

Solution

Sum =−ba=72= -\frac{b}{a} = \frac{7}{2}=−ab​=27​, product =ca=32= \frac{c}{a} = \frac{3}{2}=ac​=23​.

Δ=49−24=25\Delta = 49 - 24 = 25Δ=49−24=25, x=7±54x = \frac{7 \pm 5}{4}x=47±5​: x1=12x_1 = \frac{1}{2}x1​=21​ and x2=3x_2 = 3x2​=3. Check: 12+3=72\frac{1}{2} + 3 = \frac{7}{2}21​+3=27​ and 12⋅3=32\frac{1}{2} \cdot 3 = \frac{3}{2}21​⋅3=23​.

Exercise 3.15Test levelA system with a parameter

For which value of aaa is the system

{2x+ay=14x+6y=5\begin{cases} 2x + ay = 1 \\ 4x + 6y = 5 \end{cases}{2x+ay=14x+6y=5​

impossible? For the other values of aaa, how many solutions does it have?

Ratios of the coefficients: 24=12\frac{2}{4} = \frac{1}{2}42​=21​ for xxx, a6\frac{a}{6}6a​ for yyy, 15\frac{1}{5}51​ for the constant terms. The first two are equal if a6=12\frac{a}{6} = \frac{1}{2}6a​=21​, that is a=3a = 3a=3; in that case the ratio of the constant terms, 15\frac{1}{5}51​, is different from 12\frac{1}{2}21​ and the system is impossible. With iii the number of full-price tickets and rrr the number of reduced ones:

{i+r=12010i+6r=1000\begin{cases} i + r = 120 \\ 10i + 6r = 1000 \end{cases}{i+r=12010i+6r=1000​

Exercise 3.17Test levelThe sum of the first natural numbers

The sum of the natural numbers from 111 to nnn equals n(n+1)2\frac{n(n + 1)}{2}2n(n+1)​. For which nnn is the sum equal to 787878?

Solution

n(n+1)2=78\frac{n(n + 1)}{2} = 782n(n+1)​=78 becomes n2+n=156n^2 + n = 156n2+n=156, that is n2+n−156=0n^2 + n - 156 = 0n2+n−156=0. Δ=1+624=625=252\Delta = 1 + 624 = 625 = 25^2Δ=1+624=625=252, n=−1±252n = \frac{-1 \pm 25}{2}n=2−1±25​: n=12n = 12n=12 or n=−13n = -13n=−13. A natural number is needed: n=12n = 12n=12. Check: 12⋅132=78\frac{12 \cdot 13}{2} = 78212⋅13​=78.

#Self-check quiz

  1. What is the solution of 3(x−1)=x+53(x - 1) = x + 53(x−1)=x+5?
    3x−3=x+53x - 3 = x + 53x−3=x+5, so 2x=82x = 82x=8 and x=4x = 4x=4. The value 333 comes from forgetting to multiply the −1-1−1 by 333; the value 222 from a sign error when transposing.
  2. Solve x2−x3=2\frac{x}{2} - \frac{x}{3} = 22x​−3x​=2. What is the value of xxx?
    12
    Multiply by 666: 3x−2x=123x - 2x = 123x−2x=12, that is x=12x = 12x=12.
  3. True or false: the equation 2(x+3)=2x+62(x + 3) = 2x + 62(x+3)=2x+6 is impossible.
    Expanding you get 2x+6=2x+62x + 6 = 2x + 62x+6=2x+6, that is 0⋅x=00 \cdot x = 00⋅x=0: it is an identity, true for every xxx.
  4. The solution set of −3x+6<0-3x + 6 < 0−3x+6<0 is
    −3x<−6-3x < -6−3x<−6; dividing by −3-3−3 the direction is reversed and you get x>2x > 2x>2. The number 222 is excluded because the inequality is strict; (−∞,2)(-\infty, 2)(−∞,2) is the mistake of those who do not reverse the direction.
  5. What is the discriminant of 2x2−3x−2=02x^2 - 3x - 2 = 02x2−3x−2=0?
    25
    Δ=b2−4ac=9−4⋅2⋅(−2)=9+16=25\Delta = b^2 - 4ac = 9 - 4 \cdot 2 \cdot (-2) = 9 + 16 = 25Δ=b2−4ac=9−4⋅2⋅(−2)=9+16=25.
  6. Which numbers are solutions of x2−x−6=0x^2 - x - 6 = 0x2−x−6=0?
    One or more correct answers
    You need two numbers with sum 111 and product −6-6−6: they are 333 and −2-2−2. With −3-3−3 and 222 the sum would be −1-1−1.
  7. The inequality x2−4<0x^2 - 4 < 0x2−4<0 is satisfied for
    Roots ±2\pm 2±2, upward-opening parabola, direction <<<: inner interval. The answer x<2x < 2x<2 forgets that the numbers less than −2-2−2 also have a square greater than 444.
  8. True or false: the inequality x2+2x+3>0x^2 + 2x + 3 > 0x2+2x+3>0 is satisfied for every real xxx.
    Δ=4−12=−8<0\Delta = 4 - 12 = -8 < 0Δ=4−12=−8<0 and a=1>0a = 1 > 0a=1>0: the parabola lies entirely above the xxx-axis.
  9. What is the product of the solutions of 3x2−5x−12=03x^2 - 5x - 12 = 03x2−5x−12=0?
    -4
    Product =ca=−123=−4= \frac{c}{a} = \frac{-12}{3} = -4=ac​=3−12​=−4. Indeed the solutions are 333 and −43-\frac{4}{3}−34​.
  10. For which value of kkk does the equation x2+8x+k=0x^2 + 8x + k = 0x2+8x+k=0 have two coincident solutions?
    You need Δ=64−4k=0\Delta = 64 - 4k = 0Δ=64−4k=0, that is k=16k = 16k=16: the equation becomes (x+4)2=0(x + 4)^2 = 0(x+4)2=0.
  11. What is the solution of the system formed by x+y=7x + y = 7x+y=7 and x−y=3x - y = 3x−y=3?
    Adding the equations gives 2x=102x = 102x=10, so x=5x = 5x=5 and y=2y = 2y=2. The pair (2,5)(2, 5)(2,5) has the coordinates swapped; (4,3)(4, 3)(4,3) satisfies only the first equation and (6,3)(6, 3)(6,3) only the second.
  12. Which of these systems are impossible?
    One or more correct answers
    In the system x+y=1x + y = 1x+y=1, x+y=3x + y = 3x+y=3 the same sum would have to equal 111 and 333. In the system x+2y=3x + 2y = 3x+2y=3, 2x+4y=12x + 4y = 12x+4y=1 the coefficients are proportional (12=24\frac{1}{2} = \frac{2}{4}21​=42​) but the constant terms are not. The system with 4x−2y=24x - 2y = 24x−2y=2 is indeterminate (the second equation is twice the first); the system x−y=0x - y = 0x−y=0, x+y=2x + y = 2x+y=2 has the unique solution (1,1)(1, 1)(1,1).
  13. What is the degree of the system formed by x2y+y=1x^2y + y = 1x2y+y=1 and x−y2=0x - y^2 = 0x−y2=0?
    6
    The first equation has degree 333 (the term x2yx^2yx2y has degree 2+12 + 12+1), the second has degree 222: the degree of the system is the product 3⋅2=63 \cdot 2 = 63⋅2=6.
  14. A number added to twice itself and decreased by 555 gives 161616. The number is
    x+2x−5=16x + 2x - 5 = 16x+2x−5=16, so 3x=213x = 213x=21 and x=7x = 7x=7. The value 113\frac{11}{3}311​ comes from adding 555 instead of subtracting it; 212121 is 3x3x3x, not xxx.
  15. True or false: the system formed by 2x+4y=62x + 4y = 62x+4y=6 and x+2y=3x + 2y = 3x+2y=3 has infinitely many solutions.
    The first equation is the second multiplied by 222: they represent the same line and the system is indeterminate.
  16. Which inequality has the interval [−1,3][-1, 3][−1,3] as its solution set?
    The roots must be −1-1−1 and 333, so the factors are (x+1)(x + 1)(x+1) and (x−3)(x - 3)(x−3); you need the inner interval (direction ≤\leq≤) with the endpoints included (non-strict inequality). (x−1)(x+3)≤0(x - 1)(x + 3) \leq 0(x−1)(x+3)≤0, on the other hand, gives [−3,1][-3, 1][−3,1].
